items.abstract_or_text: How fast is AI's research taste improving? We find that the experimental research taste of frontier models has doubled every ~3 months since December 2025. items.title: @OpenAI：When possible, we want to give people a choice—and be clear about what watermarking can and can’t do. A text watermark h
items.abstract_or_text: When possible, we want to give people a choice—and be clear about what watermarking can and can’t do. A text watermark helps answer one question: “Was this likely generated by an OpenAI model?” It works by embedding an invisible statistical signal in text as it’s generated. A detector can look for this signal, and it doesn’t add visible marks or special characters. It doesn’t say who originally wrote the text or who owns it. It doesn’t identify a person, organization, account, conversation, or prompt. In our testing, watermarking hasn’t affected how capable or fast our models are, or how their responses read.

@Meta_Engineers：We're open-sourcing Rebalancer, the assignment-problem solver Meta has used for resource allocation across our infrastru
items.abstract_or_text: We're open-sourcing Rebalancer, the assignment-problem solver Meta has used for resource allocation across our infrastructure for over nine years. Given a set of objects and a set of bins, Rebalancer assigns one to the other to optimize your objectives under your constraints, including hardware placement, service and task placement, traffic routing, and more. It separates how a problem is specified from how it's stored, solved, and debugged, with both an optimal MIP solver and a parallelized local search solver. At Meta it solves ~40 million assignment problems a day across 30+ problem formulations. P99 solve time is 12 seconds on a problem with 265k objects and 3.2k bins.

items.abstract_or_text: Google DeepMind just moved protein AI from reading structures to designing chemistry. Its new system, AlphaProtein Novo, generates de novo enzymes for catalytic reactions — including enzymes that can synthesize drug-like piperidines and degrade the plasticizer DEHP, even at 90°C. The bigger story: AlphaFold learned to read proteins. AlphaProteo learned to design binders. Now AlphaProtein Novo is beginning to design catalysts. From predicting biology → writing proteins → engineering chemistry.

items.title: @percyliang：What is the probability that Astra today can generate/forecast a particular new paper past its cutoff date? Naive sampli
items.abstract_or_text: What is the probability that Astra today can generate/forecast a particular new paper past its cutoff date? Naive sampling is intractable (tail probability is astronomically small). The key idea of priced guidance is that you can lower bound this probability via a dialogue between the model (Astra) and a guide LLM (Astra with the paper), where we can precisely account for the bits of information sent from the guide to the model. One can also can think of this as a new eval for frontier models.
